title: Apollo 11 Found Clues to a Magma Ocean
title_hook: Apollo 11 Found Clues to a Magma Ocean
description: Some Apollo 11 breccias held small pieces of lunar highland crust. Scientists interpreted them as evidence for an early magma ocean. Source: Lunar and Planetary Institute — https://www.lpi.usra.edu/lunar/missions/apollo/apollo_11/samples/
narration: Apollo 11 brought back a clue: the Moon's outer layers may once have been molten. Most Apollo 11 samples were basalt and breccia, a rock made of broken fragments. Some breccias held pieces of the Moon's highland crust. Those tiny pale fragments included anorthosite, a light rock rich in plagioclase. Scientists interpreted them as evidence for an early lunar magma ocean, not a snapshot of it.
facts: Apollo 11 mainly collected basalt and breccia samples.
Some Apollo 11 breccias contained small fragments of the Moon's highland crust.
Small anorthosite fragments in breccias were interpreted as evidence for an early lunar magma ocean.
